summary.en: An Act to provide for the licensing and control of dealers in S.99/59

source.name: Attorney General's Chambers, Brunei Darussalam (AGC) — LAWS OF BRUNEI / Government Gazette

completenessNote: 来源为 AGC 官方 PDF《CAP-65-1984-ED-SECOND-HAND-DEALERS.pdf》（8 页），本次切分 14 条。该 PDF 为扫描件 + OCR 文本层，正文按版式位置重建：已剔除页眉页脚与边栏条标题、回接折行；未改写措辞、未增删内容。OCR 层面可能存在个别粘连或形近字，逐字引用请以原始 PDF 为准。

text.en: This Act may be cited as the Second-hand Dealers Short title Act. and

Act"goods" in the expression "second-hand goods" does not include any of the goods specified for the time being in the Schedule to this Act; ... "licensed dealer" means a dealer in second-hand or in such goods together with goods which are not second-hand, licensed under this Act; includes a firm or a person carrying on business in a firm's name; "shop" includes a house, place of business or other "stolen property" means property the possession whereof has been transferred by theft or extortion or robbery, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal of trust or cheating has been committed, whether the transfer has been made or the misor breach of trust or cheating has been committed within or without Brunei; but if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property. ·-(2) Every person in whose shop second-hand goods Presumpare found apparently exposed for sale or who is found in tion of second-hand goods to an unusual quantity shall be deemed, until the contrary is proved, to be a dealer 4 CAP. 65 Second-hand Dealers in second-hand goods, and no person shall be deemed to deal in second-hand goods unless he carries on business in a shop.
His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan may fit and proper person to be the licensing officer

( 1) The licensing officer may, at his discretion and on from payment of the prescribed fee, by writing exempt any ' of Act person carrying on business within the area for which he is the licensing officer from the provisions of this Act.

(2) Such exemption may be cancelled at any time by the licensing officer.

(1) No person unless exempted from this Act shall deal in second-hand goods except in accordance with the of a licence issued under this Act and in the place specified in such licence.

(2) Every licensed dealer shall keep his licence posted in a conspicuous place in his shop.

(3) Every licensed dealer shall keep exhibited at or outer door of his shop a sign-board of such size and in such position as the licensing officer directs, which signboard shall have printed thereon the words "Licensed dealer in second-hand goods."
No licensed dealer shall purchase or sell any goods before 7.00 a.m. or after 9.00 p.m.

Any person who contravenes any of the provisions of or 6 shall be guilty of an offence: Penalty, a fine of $1,000 for the first offence and a fine of $5,000 or imprisonment for 6 months for the second or any subsequent offence.

(1) Every licensed dealer shall keep in his shopof account

(a) a book legibly written in which he shall enter the particulars of all goods bought by him, with the date of purchase, the price paid for them, and the name and address of the person from whom he and such other particulars as may be

(b) a book legibly written in which he shall enter the particulars of all goods sold by him, with the date of sale, the price received for them and such other particulars as are prescribed.

(2) Such books shall be produced for examination at any time between 7.00 a.m. and 9.00 p.m. on demand by any magistrate, the licensing officer, any police officer not of sergeant or any police officer specially authorised in writing by the licensing officer to act under this Act.

(3) Any licensed dealer who fails to comply with any of this section shall be g11ilty of an offence: of $500 for the first offence and a fine of $2,500 or imprisonment for 3 months for the second or any offence.

(1) Information as to any stolen property or as to any by property which has been lost shall be given by the police as soon as possible after the theft or loss to all licensed dealers with lists and descriptions of the same.

(2) If any property answering such lists and descripthe possession of any licensed dealer or is thereafter offered to or shown to any licensed dealer, he shall, without unnecessary delay, give information to that effect at the nearest police station or to any police officer, with the name and address of the person in whose possession the was seen, and in default thereof he shall be liable on conviction to a fine of $1,000.

(3) The licensed dealer in such case may also detain the person offering or showing such property until the arrival of the police. ·'

Any police officer not below the rank of sergeant and any police officer specially authorised in writing by the licensing officer to act under this Act may enter any licensed shop at any tim~ during business hours and may warrant the shop of such licensed dealer for any property which he has reason to suspect to be therein and to be stolen property or to have been lost.

(1) Any police officer, having reason to believe that a in or loitering about a licensed dealer's shop in suspicious circumstances has with him any stolen property, may such person and require him to produce any property which he has with him.

(2) If any property is produced which the police officer has reason to suspect to be stolen property, he may take or cause to be taken the person and the property to the nearest police station there to be dealt with according to law.

(3) If any person so required to produce such property refuses to be searched, the police officer may take him or cause him to be taken before a magistrate who, if he sees or order to be searched such person and if any such property is found, may detain him with the property so found to be dealt with according to law.

(1) If any person is convicted in any court of an offence under Chapter XVII of the Penal C6de in respect of owner of any property, and it appears to the court that the same has Cap. 22 been sold to a licensed dealer, the court on proof of the of the property may, if it thinks fit, order the delivery thereof to the owner either on payment to the of the amount of the purchase price or any part thereof or without payment thereof or of any part thereof as to the court according to the conduct of the owner and the other circumstances of the case seems just and fit.

(2) The court may also adjourn the proceedings for of the licensed dealer and may summon him to attend at the adjourned hearing. -(3) If after hearing the licensed dealer the court is of opinion that he has not exercised due care in purchasing any stolen property, it may order him to pay a fine of $1,000.
